questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language and country was essential when choosing my destination. Furthermore, the modules offered persuaded me to choose the University of Leicester, compared to other universities in England.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The study abroad team had provided plenty of information before arrival and responded fast through email regarding any queries. I was also provided with a personal tutor who sent bi-weekly e-mails to check in and he could assist in finding answers to any questions I might have. The information regarding who to contact in certain situations was good, and if you did not know who to contact to get an answer, everyone was happy to help find the person who could answer.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I stayed in student accommodation so the reception provided assistance and information pamphlets. Furthermore, the university offered informational presentations regarding school facilities, COVID regulation and more.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The university provided city and village accommodation. The city accommodation was a 5-10 minute walk from campus. The village accommodation was a 15 minute bus-ride away. The university provided busses from campus to the village every 15 minutes for a reasonable fee. The prices for student accommodation varied greatly.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The accommodation was provided with a shared kitchen with up to 9 flatmates. You have to buy your own cooking supplies such as pots, pans, cutlery etc. However, the university offered a very reasonable package with all supplies you need, that can be delivered to your room upon arrival.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: In city accommodation, the quality of the rooms and facilities varied greatly. I stayed in the new buildings, which were more expensive but very nice. The cheapest options were okay, but could use some upgrades in certain areas. The accommodation is very social and provides several social events and activities where you can meet people from the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The university sends out an email with a guide on how to register for modules and other relevant information. You choose four 1st, 2nd and 3rd priorities and will be informed on which modules you get before arrival.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The guide provided all the necessary information. Otherwise, the study abroad team is quick to respond to e-mails with any questions you might have.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my first priorities.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose modules you have previously been interested in. Choose modules with an international perspective.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The professors were very competent and are great at presenting each topic in a very tangible way.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was pretty much the same as UCPH. There might be a little less reading required. The professors provided a lecture guide to each topic with a great overview of each topic. This was helpful in addition to the required reading and powerpoint.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There are more lectures than at UCPH, and there are no seminars in the same way. Usually each topic would contain a certain amount of lectures with 40-50 people and at the end of each topic we had tutorials. For the tutorials we would be 6-9 students in a room with our professor, where we had prepared a case and questions. The professor would present the case and ask questions and it was up to the students to answer. The tutorials were a great opportunity for discussions and going into depth with each topic. 
The material and books were online and free. You could also borrow the books from the library.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Family Law
Intellectual Property Law
Contract Law
Human Rights in the 21st Century

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Human Rights was very relevant and involved with current issues.
Intellectual property was a little more challenging, but the professor was very competent and good at teaching complex topics in tangible ways.

Spent more on personal spending than first anticipated.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The train to and from the airport is quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many different societies, clubs and sports. There is definitely something for everyone. Cannot recommend it enough.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I played football and futsal. The girls are so nice and welcoming to any level of skills. Once every week they hosted socials with different themes. If you want to play matches you get to travel to different cities, e.g. Oxford, Nottingham, Loughborough and so on. The football club definitely made my time in Leicester amazing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
It is quite easy to travel to London, Nottingham or Manchester or other cities using the train line.
I went to Wembley stadium and King Power stadium to watch matches. I also recommend watching football in a pub, as it is something to experience in England. Rugby is also big in Leicester and is worth going to a game even if you do not know the rules due to the atmosphere.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The people are so including, it is almost difficult not to adjust to the local culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Definitely join a society, club or sports! Participate in social events at university and the accommodation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are very nice, including, helpful and friendly. The football culture was fun to be emerged into as well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Join a society or a club.
2. Participate in tutorials
3. Make time for the social aspect of your exchange, because there is room for both studying and having fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Participate in the social events at the university and accommodation, as it is a great way to be emerged into the student life and making friends.
Enjoy it because the time goes by so fast.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social aspect! The people are great and I have definitely made friends for life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Putting myself in uncomfortable situations socially before I knew anyone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
